subject: Private deployment DPA: BYOK access limits and operator telemetry — roadmap
messages:
From: David Park <dpark@starkmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@starkmed.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy DPA + BYOK specifics

Marissa — thanks for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams are aligned that StarkMed will move forward with a private deployment (VPC-hosted control plane + on-prem model hosts) pending clarification on a couple of DPA items:

1) BYOK custody: we need a concrete statement on whether Redwood requires escrow of customer master keys (CMK) for break-glass ops, and if so the narrowest possible access window and approval process.
2) Operator telemetry: procurement flagged that any operator logs or metrics must be strictly anonymized and scoped to performance/health only — no request payload excerpts. Can you confirm the telemetry surface and retention?
3) Subprocessor list and cross-border transfers: procurement needs a current subprocessor register and any data flow map for telemetry exports outside the US.

Also attaching our standard vendor questionnaire (see procurement email). Can we get a draft DPA and a short one-page summary of operator access constraints by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
David Park
VP, IT Security
StarkMed Health

Attachment: starkmed-subproc-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf, 480KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Park <dpark@starkmed.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA + BYOK specifics

David — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, more detail below and a draft attached.

1) Key escrow: Redwood does NOT require long-term escrow of customer CMKs for private deployments. We offer an emergency-only escrow process that is customer-initiated, requires a signed escalation request from your security officer and a two-person Redwood approvals chain. The maximum break-glass window is documented as 72 hours and is auditable. We are open to carving this into the DPA as an optional addendum.

2) Operator telemetry: we will provide a restrictive telemetry profile for private deployments: aggregated GPU/host health, queue lengths, and anonymized error rates. No raw request payloads, no prompt/response snippets, and no customer identifiers in logs. Retention by default is 30 days for metrics and 90 days for operational traces; we can shorten retention to 7 days on the private offering for StarkMed.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: attached is the current subprocessor register and a dataflow diagram showing that telemetry exports are only to our control plane for health aggregation; we can ensure region-limited endpoints and disable any cross-border exports by contract.

Deliverables I'm attaching: redwood-private-deploy-dpa-draft.pdf (DPA + annexes) and operator-telemetry-limits.xlsx (mapping of telemetry types to retention and scrub rules).

Next steps:
- Please review the DPA draft and mark redlines.
- If procurement wants a shorter one-pager, Ben will draft the executive summary focused on operator access and limited telemetry.
- Propose a joint call Wed 10am PT with your security team and our engineering leads to walk the technical appendix.

Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-dpa-draft.pdf, operator-telemetry-limits.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2029 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA + BYOK specifics — technical appendix suggestions

Following up with technical constraints we should propose for the appendix (for the Wed call):

- BYOK model: recommended pattern is customer-held CMK in their KMS with Redwood-held ephemeral session keys. Root key never leaves customer KMS. We support HSM-backed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CloudKMS, Azure KeyVault) and on-prem Hardware Security Modules.
- Escrow flow: if an emergency escrow is accepted, use sealed envelope in a third-party key-escrow custodian. Access requires an emergency ticket, two-member Redwood approvals, and explicit customer authorization recorded in the ticket. All escrow access is logged and shipped as hashed audit records to customer’s SIEM on request.
- Operator telemetry rubric (suggested):
  * Level 0: Mandatory anonymized metrics (host CPU/GPU temp, queue depth) — retention default 30d, min 7d
  * Level 1: Traces (no payloads, only timing/latency histograms) — redact request identifiers; retention default 90d, can be set to 7d for StarkMed
  * Forbidden: any payload, prompt/response fragments, PII, PHI excerpts
- Subprocessor visibility: provide an up-to-date register and commit to 30-day notice before adding any new cross-border telemetry processors; allow customer to object and require mitigation.

I attached a short checklist we can share with procurement. Happy to drive the tech appendix on the Wed call.

Irene Choi
Director, Product Security
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: tech-appendix-checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 56KB)

From: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@starkmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Park <dpark@starkmed.com>, Procurement <procurement@starkmed.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2029 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy DPA + BYOK specifics — next steps

Marissa / Irene — this is very helpful, thank you. A few quick items from procurement/security after reviewing the attachments:

- Confirmed: StarkMed will accept an emergency-only escrow addendum if the access window and approval workflow are contractual and auditable. Please add explicit escalation steps in the DPA Appendix.
- Telemetry: the proposed rubric looks acceptable. We will request the 7-day retention option for traces and metrics in the final DPA.
- Subprocessors: procurement wants the subprocessor register as a live Drive folder with a timestamped change-log. Can Redwood commit to keeping that folder current and notifying us 30 days before any new cross-border telemetry processor is added?

Action items / timeline:
1) Redwood to update DPA draft with: escrow addendum language, explicit operator approvals, and a one-page operator-access summary for our CISO. (Marissa / Ben) — by EOD Friday (5 Jul).
2) Redwood security to produce the technical appendix and the live subprocessor Drive folder link prior to the call. (Irene / Karthik) — by Thu EOD.
3) Schedule 45-min technical review on Fri 6 Jul — David and two engineers from StarkMed; please send calendar invite.

If you can also include a short note on audit evidence (SOC 2 report window and how Redwood will share samples), that would help procurement close the review. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Lara Gomez
Director, Procurement Technology
StarkMed Health
